subject: Evidence sync: subprocessor roster, CAIQ export & KMS residency details

From: Sara Doyle <sara.doyle@medsecure.com>

Cc: MedSecure Risk Team <risk@medsecure.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T08:12:00Z
Subject: Evidence sync: subprocessor roster, CAIQ export & KMS residency details

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement and security review we need the following artifacts from Redwood to finish the SIG/CAIQ intake for the MedSecure deployment:

1) A current subprocessor roster (CSV) that includes: provider name, role (e.g., telemetry, KMS, compute), country of residence, and contract date.
2) CAIQ export (JSON or spreadsheet) or SIG Lite filled out for the current production-surface models.
3) KMS residency and key custody mapping (which KMS provider holds keys for which data flows, and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed).
4) Any attestation or onboarding evidence for onshore-only subprocessors (we may need an onshore residency attestation).

We'd like to get the files by EOD Aug 6 (US Eastern) to keep our procurement timeline. If anything is gated, please flag what needs legal review or redaction.

Happy to schedule a short walkthrough once you've uploaded the bundle — I'm copying Risk so they can weigh in on key residency questions.

Thanks,
Sara Doyle
Lead Information Security
MedSecure Health

Attachment: none (we'll accept the CSV/CAIQ upload link)

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a coordinated package. Plan below:

- I'll attach a SIG-lite spreadsheet (named redwood_sig_lite_v1.xlsx) with answers scoped to our inference surface and the CAIQ questions that typically overlap.
- Attached is a machine-readable subprocessor manifest (subprocessor_manifest_20260805.csv) with provider, function, legal entity, country, and the contract/PO date.
- Aditya will supply a KMS mapping (kms_key_map.csv) with residency and whether keys are customer- or Redwood-managed.
- Marcus will flag any vendors that require onshore attestations or extra contractual language.

Timeline: we will send the three files in this thread within the next 6 hours and can join a 30-min walkthrough on Aug 6 between 13:00–16:00 ET if that works. If you need earlier, let us know.

Delivery notes / caveats:
- We redact internal email addresses for contractors in the CSV but include vendor legal names and jurisdiction.
- For a small set of telemetry vendors we route telemetry via a partner ingress; residency is listed as the partner’s legal domicile.

Attachments: redwood_sig_lite_v1.xlsx (SIG-lite), subprocessor_manifest_20260805.csv (CSV)

Best,

Subject: Re: Evidence sync: subprocessor roster, CAIQ export & KMS residency details

Hi all —

I've attached the KMS mapping (kms_key_map.csv) and added short notes inline in the manifest. Summary of residency / custody model:

- Customer-managed encryption keys (recommended for regulated customers): we offer a customer KMS integration that supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For MedSecure we can support customer keys in us-east-1 (AWS) or europe-west1 (GCP) depending on which tenancy they prefer.
- Redwood-managed keys: used for self-serve hosted instances only and are region-scoped (us-west-2 for US tenants, eu-west-1 for EU tenants). Keys are rotated every 90 days; rotation events are logged in our audit stream (we can include audit log samples).
- Ephemeral session keys: for model-serving workers we generate ephemeral symmetric keys per-session that are wrapped by the KMS key. These are short-lived (TTL ~ 24 hours) and never leave the host in plaintext.

Notes for the CSV: I've added two special-case vendors that require onshore residency attestations (listed in column 'residency_note'). Marcus — those two will need the contractual language you mentioned.

Attachments: kms_key_map.csv

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
